title: Active Learning Surrogates for Integrating Electron Microscopy and Computational Insights from Simulations in Autonomous Experiments
problem: Bridging the gap between simulations and experiments due to disparities in time and scale makes it difficult to estimate properties like energy and electronic states from microscopic images and to provide feedback based on theoretical insights.
motivation: Accelerating scientific discovery across technology and pharmaceuticals by integrating AI with simulations and experiments.
method: The approach trains machine learning models (deep kernel methods, a technique for learning patterns from data) on microscopic images to predict differences in defect formation energy for various structures. It starts by fully training on simulated images to establish a baseline, then uses active learning (strategically picking examples that are either hard to predict or energetically interesting) to predict what structures appear at key points along simulated trajectories, reducing data and computational needs. The system uses an autoencoder-decoder neural network—which compresses images to extract essential features—to precisely align simulations with real experimental observations.
key_novelty: Deep kernel-based surrogate models combined with active learning map microscopic images to defect formation energy differences while strategically selecting which simulation paths to analyze, reducing data and computational requirements.
contributions: Deep kernel-based surrogate models for mapping microscopic images to defect formation energies
Active learning strategy reducing data requirements and simulation time through uncertainty-based sampling
Autoencoder-decoder latent space model for feature extraction and molecular structure reconstruction
Autonomous experiment steering through computationally guided trajectory prediction

metrics.other: reconstruction loss ~0.2, time-to-solution comparable to experimental measurements

primary_theme: Active learning surrogates for autonomous experiments
